briefs.headline: Denmark explores Bengaluru’s digital talent to bridge skills gap
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Facing a growing shortage of skilled technology professionals that threatens its digital ambitions and global competitiveness, Denmark is looking to deepen its partnership with India and tap its massive digital talent pool including Bengaluru.
Denmark’s foreign affairs minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen, who was in Bengaluru, launched the report titled “Access to Tech Talent in India” Friday. Published by Innovation Centre Denmark (ICDK), Bengaluru, it highlighted how India’s expanding technology workforce, strong higher education ecosystem and growing research and development (R&D) capabilities could help Denmark address its talent crunch.
“Denmark and 
Karnataka
 both understand that innovation is key to our prosperity. You have an enormous talent pool with exactly the skills that Danish companies are looking for. We are not the only ones trying to attract Indian talent. So, we also want to make Denmark an attractive place for skilled Indian professionals to go for work,” he said.
Citing Danish Society of Engineers, the report said Denmark could face a shortage of about 20,400 STEM graduates by 2040 if current trends continued. IT specialists comprise 5.8% of Denmark’s workforce, against its 2030 target of 7.7%. European Union’s corresponding target is 10%.
In 2024, about 33% of Danish IT companies reported specialist vacancies they could not fill. An ageing population and a low unemployment rate of 2.9% in Aug 2025 further constrained domestic talent availability.
Denmark recorded a net gain of only slightly more than 100 digital professionals in 2024, as foreign arrivals were largely offset by departures, mostly because their partners struggled to find jobs, the report said.
It said Danish organisations could drive growth and innovation by engaging with India in innovation and R&D, capability building and sustainable governance. Danish firms could join Indo–Danish calls, collaborate with India’s 25 Technology Innovation Hubs and use Manthan for industry-academia matchmaking and co-funding opportunities.

stories.headline: 98% of company resolutions pass despite institutional investor dissent: Report
stories.bodyText:
High promoter shareholding of over 55% in listed companies continues to blunt the ability of institutional investors to challenge management-proposed resolutions, with an overwhelming 98% of resolutions that attracted significant institutional dissent still getting passed in the first half of 2026-27, according to a Prime Database report. The trend raises questions about the effectiveness of shareholder voting at annual general meetings (AGMs), with the voices of institutional investors and public shareholders often unable to influence decisions.
Despite institutional investors voting against more than 20% of the votes on 1,514 resolutions during the April-September period, 1,480 of these proposals secured shareholder approval, underscoring the limits of dissent in companies where promoters command a dominant share of voting rights, Prime Database said.
The data from the proxy season, compiled by primeinfobase.com, an initiative of Prime Database Group, points to a structural weakness in shareholder democracy. Opposition from institutional investors may raise questions over governance, board appointments, executive remuneration and related-party transactions, but is often unable to stop resolutions from being passed.
Dissent trends
Across companies listed on the NSE main board, resolutions attracting dissent from more than 20% of institutional shareholders declined marginally to 12.60%, or 1,514 of the 12,016 resolutions for which institutional voting data was available. This compared with 12.73% in the corresponding period last year, 15.66% in 2024-25 and a peak of 17.43% in 2023-24, the report said.
As of March 31, 2026, promoters held 55% of the shares in NSE-listed companies, compared with 11% held by institutional investors and 23% by individual investors. The remaining 11% was held by other non-institutional, non-individual investors, Pranav Haldea, managing director of Prime Database Group, said.
Board appointments and remuneration continued to attract the most institutional dissent, he said, adding that investors often question the independence of directors, while excessive promoter and executive remuneration remains a contentious issue.
The concentration of voting power among promoters is also reflected in participation levels. Promoters voted nearly 95% of their holdings, while other non-institutional public shareholders voted only 15% of their holdings, indicating considerable apathy among this segment, Haldea said.
In Nifty-50 companies, resolutions attracting more than 20% institutional dissent declined sharply to 5%, or 20 resolutions, in the first half of 2026-27, compared with 9%, or 54 resolutions, in the corresponding period last year and 11% in 2024-25.
RPT scrutiny
Related-party transactions (RPTs) continued to be a key area of scrutiny. As many as 1,521 RPT resolutions were proposed in the first half of 2026-27, 23% more than the 1,241 in the corresponding period last year and nearly seven times the 220 recorded in the first half of 2020-21.
Of these, 135 resolutions, or 9%, attracted opposition from more than 20% of institutional investors, but only 17, or 1%, were defeated. Dissent on RPTs has declined since these transactions require a majority-of-minority vote, the report said.
Domestic mutual funds voted in favour of 88% of resolutions and against 12% during the first half of 2026-27. Their support for management proposals has declined from 93% in 2021-22, following Sebi’s mandatory voting requirement. LIC, India’s largest institutional investor, voted in favour of 98% of resolutions, against 1% and abstained on 1%.
Prime Database said a total of 15,977 resolutions were proposed across 3,235 shareholder meetings involving 2,295 NSE-listed companies in the first half of 2026-27, down 4% from 16,692 resolutions in 2,967 meetings involving 2,124 companies in the corresponding period last year. Nearly all resolutions were management-proposed — 15,976 — with just one resolution proposed by a shareholder.

stories.headline: Retailers pitch big buys on Black Friday
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU/DELHI: Indian retailers are using Black Friday to draw shoppers back between Diwali and the year-end sales. Once largely online, the sale now extends to malls and electronics stores, with offers ranging from designer handbags to appliance bundles costing nearly Rs 1.5 lakh.
Early sales at Nexus Select Malls point to growth in the low teens in fashion, beauty and accessories, said Nishank Joshi, its chief marketing officer. Electronics sales were growing steadily, though it was too early to tell whether shoppers were spending more per visit than last year.
DLF Retail expects its malls to draw double-digit growth in footfalls over a regular weekend, said Pushpa Bector, its group executive director and business head. She estimated a 15-20% increase in sales across its retail partners.
In Delhi, Vijay Sales advertised appliance packages from Rs 49,990 to Rs 1,49,990. The cheapest included a TV, fridge and washing machine. Reliance Digital advertised the iPhone 17 Pro from Rs 54,990 after an in-store discount, a handset trade-in, an exchange bonus and cashback.
Croma advertised Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra at Rs 85,999, including the exchange value of a Galaxy S25 Ultra. 
Lifestyle advertised discounts of up to 50% from Nov 25 to 29.
“We see the biggest opportunity in premium electronics, appliances, furniture and luxury, where consumers often decide what to buy well ahead and wait for a good deal,” said Anand Ramanathan, partner and consumer industry leader at Deloitte South Asia.
In Deloitte’s March 2026 survey, 65% of Indian respondents were willing to make a large non-essential purchase, down five percentage points from February. Only 43% felt they could afford the things that brought them joy.
Tata CLiQ’s sale began on Nov 19. CEO Gopal Asthana said daily business had doubled compared with regular days and he expected it to exceed three times the usual level over the weekend. He expects 30% growth over last year’s Black Friday at Tata CLiQ Luxury, where watches, apparel and footwear were most popular.
Coach’s India site listed its Brooklyn Shoulder Bag 39 at Rs 37,500 against a reference price of Rs 62,500. Charles & Keith offered up to 40% off selected handbags and shoes. Tom Ford Beauty and Bobbi Brown placed less emphasis on the event, an industry expert said.
At handbag brand Miraggio, two days of a buy-one-get-one offer on its website generated about twice the sales and more than 2.5 times the orders of last year’s 10-day buy-two-get-one promotion, said founder and CEO Mohit Jain. On marketplaces, its average order value rose 2-5% from last year.
Around 30% of styles sold during the event come from new collections, a Myntra spokesperson said, citing demand for winter clothing and wedding wear. GoKwik’s network recorded 5.8 lakh online orders worth Rs 90 crore by 8.53 pm on Friday, averaging Rs 1,551 per order.
“The weeks that follow give us a better read on how much demand the weekend added and how much it brought forward,” Joshi said.

stories.headline: Thumbs-up for nutrition labelling push
stories.bodyText:
JAIPUR/NEW DELHI: In his first comments since the US Trade Representative announced its move to levy up to 25% additional tariffs on Indian exports, commerce minister 
Piyush Goyal
 Friday said the trade deal with the US is close to culmination.
“The process and pathway, which was always something, which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape,” he said at an event. While talks have been underway for 20 months, India’s trade ties have come under repeated pressure due to Trump’s tariff policy, dotted with flip-flops and with no consistency. Govt has been trudging with caution, seeking to ensure that the country’s interests are protected, without annoying the Trump administration, which had slapped 50% additional tariffs on Indian exports.
“Our talks with the US are continuing. The US is our largest trade partner with exports of over $90 billion. It is an important market. We should be holding discussions with them and we should prepare for an FTA that offers a mutually win-win solution,” commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal told reporters in Jaipur without offering any timeline for finalising a trade deal.
The US has proposed 25% additional tariffs following two section 301 investigations, and offered to lower it to 17% in case India signed a trade deal. 
In the past Goyal and Agrawal have has stated on multiple occasions that the groundwork for a trade deal has been done and it can be signed once the US tariff framework is in place, provided India gets a comparative advantage over its rivals such as China, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Sri Lanka and Pakistan.
Asked if the proposed tariffs on India were unfair, Agrawal said: “They have their own tariff policy and I would not like to discuss that. Section 301 is an instrument available with them, which has in the past also been used to investigate and levy tariffs. Now they have conducted investigation against 16 countries and given a draft notification. We are examining it and we will file our response. The final notification will come after hearing us.”

stories.headline: Cotton output shortfall: SIMA seeks five-year import duty waiver
stories.bodyText:
The textile industry has called for a five-year exemption from import duty on cotton to address a widening gap between domestic production and consumption, and enable Indian mills to capitalise on opportunities arising from Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).
Cotton production in the current marketing season, which began on October 1, is projected at 248.66 lakh bales, significantly below the textile industry’s estimated requirement of 350-360 lakh bales, the Southern India Mills’ Association (SIMA) said.
Cotton consumption rose from 323 lakh bales in 2024-25 cotton season to 340 lakh bales last cotton year, supported by duty-free import of 72 lakh bales. Another 15-20 lakh bales of duty-free imports are expected by the end of December.
Atul Ganatra, former president of the Cotton Association of India, said imports this season may be almost 90 lakh bales to meet the demand. The arrivals so far since October 1 is just about 41 lakh bales compared with 65 lakh bales for the corresponding period last year.
The SIMA chairman Durai Palaniswamy said the Prime Minister should intervene and remove the import duty on cotton for five years so that the textile industry gains from the market opportunities emerging because of the Free Trade Agreements.

stories.headline: Have asked Centre to let us invest in airlines, facilitate their development: Adani Group CFO
stories.bodyText:
The Adani group has sought the government’s permission to allow it to invest in airlines, the conglomerate’s chief financial officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh said Friday. This is the first public confirmation by a senior Adani official of the group’s interest in investing in the airline sector. The diversified Adani group is the operator of eight airports in India, including the country’s second-busiest airport Mumbai.
According to Singh, India’s domestic aviation market has the potential to have 30,000 daily flights, against roughly 3,200-3,200 at present. “And that’s why we requested the government to at least allow us to invest, so that we can facilitate the development of airlines. Some fund, some other airline company and things like that…or an entrepreneur who wants to go into that space,” Singh said on the sidelines of an industry event. He didn’t name any airline as a potential investment opportunity.
The government has been calling for more airlines in the Indian skies, given the duopoly of IndiGo and the Air India group, which have a cumulative domestic market share of over 90%. But allowing airport operators to run airlines can have pitfalls, specifically those related to fair competition and non-discriminatory access to carriers, according to experts.
To be sure, there is no blanket policy restricting airport operators from holding substantial equity in airlines, although cross-holding restrictions are part of contracts for some airports operated by private sector players, like in the case of Mumbai airport. In August, the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) informed Parliament that the state-owned Airports Authority of India (AAI) had received a request seeking a waiver of the cross-holding cap provision, but didn’t name the Adani group.
In a letter addressed to the AAI chairman in June, Adani Airport Holdings’s CEO Arun Bansal had sought a waiver or clarification in the Mumbai airport’s operation, management and development agreement (OMDA) to pave the way for the group to directly or indirectly invest in, acquire, promote, or control a scheduled airline, it is learnt. However, the conglomerate’s falship Adani Enterprises had informed stock exchanges in July that it was not evaluating any proposal to enter the airline business.
As per the OMDA for Mumbai and Delhi airports, scheduled airlines and their group entities can’t hold more than 10% stake in the airport operator. This also effectively restricts the airport operator and its group entities from investing in or promoting a scheduled airline. The Adani group has 74% stake in the Mumbai airport, while GMR has 74% in the Delhi airport.
In September, Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu had said that the government will weigh all the pros and cons and will focus on maintaining market balance while deciding on the issue of cross-ownership between airlines and airports. Naidu added that no decision had been taken and the matter was under deliberation. Sources had earlier indicated that the Adani group was weighing having its own airline and MoCA was learnt to have initiated preliminary discussions internally. Any change on this front will also require the approval of the Union Cabinet, they had said.
According to industry insiders and experts, if the Adani group indeed moved ahead with a plan to run an airline, there is bound to be stiff resistance from existing airlines and other stakeholders due to potential conflict of interest situations. These could include preferential treatment and slot allocation to the airline opened by the operator.
IndiGo’s Managing Director Rahul Bhatia had said in July that any move by the government to allow airport operators to own airlines will create a “massive conflict of interest” and will be against the interest of consumers. “We are reading news as you are. All I can say is that, if the news has any merit, one, it has no global precedent…and typically (it will create) a massive conflict of interest. Over a period of time, it would actually be against the interest of consumers,” Bhatia had said following reports of the Adani group’s interest in the airline business.
In his letter to the AAI chief, Bansal wrote that airport neutrality can be preserved through existing and enhanced safeguards like International Air Transport Association (IATA)-compliant slot allocation process and oversight from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), and Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India (AERA), and MoCA, it it learnt.
Additionally, safeguards like transparent and non-discriminatory airport operating procedures, information barriers and ring-fencing arrangements, independent governance structures, and regulatory monitoring and compliance mechanisms would help ensure airport neutrality and non-discriminatory access, Bansal is understood to have written.
Apart from being a large airport operator, the Adani group has a major presence in other segments of the aviation sector, including ground handling, maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), and pilot training. The conglomerate also plans to set up an aircraft manufacturing facility in India in partnership with Brazil’s Embraer.
In the letter to the AAI chairman, Bansal is understood to have written that allowing the waiver would facilitate the emergence of an additional large-scale airline, thereby enhancing competition and reducing market concentration risks, apart from enhancing regional connectivity.
The airline sector in India has seen a number of airlines fail due to a difficult operating environment, fierce competition in a highly price-sensitive market, and global supply chain woes. The government wants strong corporate groups with deep pockets to foray into the sector given the challenging operating environment in the world’s fastest-growing major aviation market.
Notably, Jeet Adani, who looks after the conglomerate’s aviation business, had said in December last year that the Adani group was not interested in the airline business as running a carrier didn’t fit the group’s capital discipline and philosophy, which was about investing in assets in high-margin businesses and sweating those assets. The airline business is the opposite of that, Jeet Adani had said in a televised interview.
But the thought process might have changed since then, largely due to two factors — the government’s push for more airlines in a bid to increase competition and check market concentration, and Adani’s own venture to set up a final assembly line (FAL) of Embraer’s passenger jets.
-With inputs from PTI

briefs.headline: Sensex falls 989 points as investors book profits

briefs.headline: RBI eases CRR stance amid liquidity squeeze
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: 
RBI
 has reversed its Oct 9 liquidity-tightening measure, reducing banks’ daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) maintenance to a minimum of 90% of the statutory requirement from 99%. The earlier increase was intended to absorb surplus liquidity generated by inflows under the special FCNR(B) deposit scheme.
The rollback comes as banking system liquidity tightens and credit growth continues to outpace deposit mobilisation. Bank credit grew 19.3% year-on-year in the fortnight ended Nov 15, 2026, against deposit growth of 16.4%, widening the gap to 290 basis points from 140 basis points a year earlier.
Banks face sustained pressure to rely on higher-cost wholesale funding and borrowings to maintain lending momentum, with incremental credit absorbing over 96% of incremental deposits in FY27 and the deposits-advances gap narrowing to Rs 66,495 crore. SCB borrowings rose by Rs 2,86,022 crore in FY27 so far, against a contraction of Rs 80,264 crore in the same period of FY26.
Both deposits and credit contracted during the fortnight, but deposits showed a relatively sharper fall. Aggregate deposits declined Rs 2,04,150 crore (0.7%) to Rs 280.5 lakh crore, with demand deposits falling Rs 1,23,526 crore and time deposits Rs 80,625 crore. Credit fell Rs 71,139 crore (0.3%) to Rs 231.1 lakh crore.

briefs.headline: Many FTA benefits untapped: RBI
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Indian exporters are leaving much of the benefit of the country’s expanding free-trade network untapped, with only 20-30% of eligible shipments using preferential tariffs against 60-70% in partner countries, 
RBI
 governor Sanjay Malhotra said. As a result, 70-80% of eligible Indian exports continue to enter partner markets under regular most-favoured-nation (MFN) tariffs, making them less competitive than goods from countries that use trade agreements more effectively.
India has trade agreements with UAE, Australia, EFTA, Oman, UK, Asean, Japan and South Korea, offering lower or zero import duties on eligible goods. Yet exporters, particularly smaller firms, have failed to fully claim these benefits. “It is an opportunity we are leaving on the table,” he said.
Speaking at the SME Finance & Investment Summit here on Friday, Malhotra urged MSMEs to break out of a low-growth trap by investing in technology, raising productivity, formalising operations and expanding overseas. He outlined a five-point action plan for businesses and called on lenders to combine digital data with relationship-based banking to widen access to credit.
The challenge begins with scale. About 99% of Indian MSMEs remain micro-enterprises, with few graduating into large businesses. The transition rate is far below that in Australia (44%), Israel (42%), Indonesia (31%) and Poland (30%). “By one estimate, only about 10% of India’s large companies in 2022 had been MSMEs at any point after 2000... 
Too many of our firms are born small and stay small,” Malhotra said.
One deterrent has been the fear of losing regulatory concessions and subsidies upon crossing the thresholds for MSME classification. Govt has raised these limits to reduce that disincentive. But size is only part of the problem. Value added per worker in Indian MSMEs is just 26% of the level in large domestic enterprises, leaving them behind both advanced economies and emerging-market peers such as Brazil and Mexico.
 Raising productivity to the global top-quartile level could add 11% to India’s GDP.
Technology adoption is another weakness. AI penetration among Indian MSMEs is estimated at 15%, below China, the US and Germany. Although 76% of MSME leaders use AI in some form, only 5% have embedded it in core operations. Informality compounds the problem: inadequate bookkeeping, delayed tax filings and cash transactions leave lenders with little reliable information on business cash flows, forcing them to depend on physical collateral.

briefs.headline: Adani may take stake in existing airline or back startup, says group CFO
briefs.deck: Adani Group has expressed its intention to invest in the airline industry to support growth and expansion. The group's CFO mentioned that India's aviation market has significant untapped potential, with approximately 60 crore potential passengers. Current government regulations limit the group's equity stake in scheduled airlines, prompting a request for an exemption. They aim to enhance…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Adani Group
 confirmed Friday it is keen to be in the airline business by investing in an existing carrier or supporting entrepreneurs who are planning to launch startup carriers. It is learned that the group is not looking at launching an airline of its own.
Speaking on the sidelines of a summit, Adani Group CFO Jugeshinder (Robbie) Singh said: “We would like to invest in airlines because India has about 60 crore more people who can fly. Today, we have roughly 3,200-3,300 flights a day. India should have 30,000 flights a day. We need to do what we can to get the country there...”
As recently as Sept 24, Adani Airports CEO Arun Bansal had said the company is in the airport business and does not want to compete with its customer airlines.
Government restriction on holding more than 10 per cent equity in airlines
Government’s PPP agreements with operators of Delhi and Mumbai airports restrict them from holding more than 10 per cent equity in a scheduled airline. Adani Group, which runs both the Mumbai and Navi Mumbai airports, apart from six others in India as of now, has sought exemption from this clause.
When the exemption request was made on June 4, 2026, it was speculated that Adani wants to start an airline. In a stock exchange filing in July, the group denied “speculation suggesting that Adani Enterprises is planning to launch an airline”. 
GMR Group, which runs Delhi’s IGI Airport among others, is watching Adani’s moves closely.
“We’d like to invest so that much faster growth is possible, and facilities can be made available to the 60 crore people who can fly but don’t because the routes are not there. Sometimes you hear the noise about Mumbai, Navi Mumbai airport and so on. For us, when we build airport infrastructure, that 60 crore potential passenger base is what’s important,” Singh said.
“We’ve built the infrastructure. Now airlines also have to speed up. That’s why we requested government to at least allow us to invest so we can facilitate the development of airlines,” he added.

briefs.headline: SDTT files caveats against Venu Srinivasan, Vijay Singh
briefs.deck: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust has filed caveats following complaints from vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh regarding a lawsuit. They are seeking regulatory hearings to resolve these issues before any subsequent actions occur. This comes on the heels of previous apprehensions voiced by the vice-chairmen on trustee appointments and matters involving Tata Sons, which previously hindered…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: A day after Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and 
Vijay Singh
 separately complained to Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC) over the trust’s decision to sue 
Tata Sons
, SDTT filed two caveats, one against each. It sought a hearing before the regulator takes any action against it. The caveats were among the first matters MCC took up on Friday, ahead of Bombay high court hearing in SDTT’s suit against Tata Sons.
Srinivasan and Singh objected to SDTT’s Nov 25 resolution, passed by a majority over their dissent, authorising legal action against Tata Sons. Among their concerns was that the relief sought could impede Tata Sons’ RBI-mandated listing.
This is not the first time caveats have been filed in response to complaints by Srinivasan and Singh. In late Sept, the vice-chairmen sought an MCC inquiry into SDTT’s trustee appointments and its involvement in Tata Sons affairs. SDTT chairman Noel Tata and his son and trustee Neville Tata then filed caveats before MCC, the city civil court and Bombay high court.
The latest caveats also reflect an earlier episode. On April 28, Srinivasan complained to MCC that Sir Ratan Tata Trust’s board composition breached a rule capping permanent trustees at one-fourth of its total strength. SRTT said it learnt of the complaint only on May 15, when MCC issued an ex parte order barring board meetings pending an inquiry.
The restriction has since left SRTT unable to take board decisions and contributed to the adjournment of Tata Sons’ AGM for lack of quorum.

briefs.headline: Minority shareholders’ interest protection a key priority: Sebi
briefs.deck: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey highlighted the priority of protecting minority shareholders amid concerns regarding the Tata Steel-APL Apollo transaction. The structure and valuation of the deal have raised questions from proxy advisory firms, necessitating further review. Tata Steel plans to acquire a significant stake in APL Apollo Tubes while simultaneously selling its steel businesses. Sebi…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Amid concerns raised by minority shareholders in the proposed Tata Steel-APL Apollo transaction, Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey Friday said safeguarding the interests of the minority shareholders is a key priority for the market regulator.
“Minority shareholders’ interest is very important for Sebi. Investor protection is key. We are looking at it (the Tata - APL deal)... because in any case, a takeover is involved, an offer is involved,” Pandey told reporters in response to a query regarding the proposed deal.
The remarks assume significance in the wake of the concerns raised by proxy advisory firms over the proposed transaction’s structure, valuation and safeguards for minority shareholders of APL Apollo.
On Monday, 
Tata Steel
 announced an agreement to acquire the entire 26.6 per cent promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes for Rs 15,510 crore and plans to take over another 26 per cent through an open offer of Rs 16,756 crore. APL Apollo, meanwhile, is simultaneously buying Tata Steel’s tubes and colour-coated steel businesses for Rs 28,000 crore.
Sebi is yet to receive the revised contours of the transaction, and the regulator would await the revised proposal before taking further steps. 
Under the takeover regulations, the draft letter of offer is generally required to be filed within five working days of the public announcement.
At an Assocham event, Pandey also said Sebi is aiming to reduce the onboarding time for FPIs from several months to as little as five business days through digital workflows and system integration and bringing India’s regulatory framework closer to global standards.
He also said that the regulator is undertaking a comprehensive review of the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) framework to eliminate disclosures that result in duplication with filings made with the corporate affairs ministry, while also planning to replace multiple stock exchange fines for the same compliance lapse with a single penalty.
Sebi is also reviewing the Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR) framework governing initial public offerings (IPOs), follow-on public offerings (FPOs), preferential issues and qualified institutional placements (QIPs).
For stock brokers, the regulator is exploring a graded compliance framework under which regulatory obligations would be aligned with a broker’s scale, the exposure that clients have and dependence on technology.

briefs.headline: US goods trade deficit hits $149.5 billion as AI infrastructure imports surge to record
briefs.deck: The US goods trade deficit surged by 10.7% in October, reaching $149.5 billion. A significant driver was the 6.1% increase in imports, largely attributed to capital goods essential for artificial intelligence infrastructure. Exports also rose, climbing 3.2% to $215.8 billion. However, reflecting these trade trends, Goldman Sachs lowered its fourth-quarter GDP growth projection to 2.2%…
briefs.bodyText:
The US goods trade deficit widened sharply in October as imports of AI-related infrastructure and other goods surged to a record high, potentially weighing on economic growth in the fourth quarter.
The goods trade deficit increased 10.7 per cent, or $14.4 billion, to $149.5 billion in October, the highest level since March 2025, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters had expected a deficit of $133 billion.
Imports jumped 6.1 per cent, or $21.1 billion, to a record $365.3 billion, the highest since the government began tracking the series in 1992. The increase was led by capital goods, which surged 8.5 per cent during the month and 80 per cent year-on-year, reflecting heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Imports also rose across motor vehicles, industrial supplies and consumer goods, indicating strong domestic demand despite President Donald Trump's aggressive tariffs.
"The trade deficit in goods worsened in October, which will take a toll on economic growth in the fourth quarter," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS, as quoted by Reuters. "Capital goods imports are surging, showing that AI doesn't always lead to greater US economic growth."
Exports of goods increased 3.2 per cent, or $6.7 billion, to $215.8 billion in October.
The surge in AI-related imports could limit the technology's contribution to economic growth, despite strong corporate investment.
"This year's surge in capital goods imports is one reason why AI is adding less to GDP than corporate spending figures suggest," economists at Goldman Sachs wrote in a note.
Trade had already subtracted 3.21 percentage points from US GDP growth in the third quarter, according to government data released on Wednesday. The drag was offset by strong consumer spending and business investment, particularly in AI-related equipment. The economy expanded at an annualised rate of 4.3 per cent in the third quarter, following 2.2 per cent growth in the previous quarter.
Meanwhile, wholesale inventories rose 0.9 per cent in October after increasing 0.8 per cent in September, while retail inventories climbed 0.8 per cent following a 0.7 per cent rise in the previous month.
Goldman Sachs economists lowered their fourth-quarter GDP growth estimate by 0.2 percentage point to 2.2 per cent, factoring in the October trade and inventory data.

briefs.headline: RBI Governor pegs AI’s potential economic value to MSMEs at $685 billion, urges faster adoption
briefs.deck: “This is entirely doable,” the Governor said, encouraging enterprises to begin with practical applications such as digital accounting, inventory management, quality control and customer engagement before expanding their use of AI.
briefs.bodyText:
Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption could unlock economic value of $490-685 billion for India’s micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), but with only around 15% of the country’s small businesses currently using the technology, the sector risks missing out on substantial productivity gains, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra said on Friday.
Speaking at the SME Finance and Investment Summit in Mumbai, Mr. Malhotra urged MSMEs to accelerate the adoption of AI, technology and innovation to improve competitiveness and bridge the productivity gap with larger enterprises.
AI could help smaller businesses compete with larger players in terms of speed, quality and personalisation, he said, noting that India’s adoption rate lagged behind countries such as China, the U.S. and Germany.
“This is entirely doable,” the Governor said, encouraging enterprises to begin with practical applications such as digital accounting, inventory management, quality control and customer engagement before expanding their use of AI.
He stressed that technology adoption must be supported by investments in workforce skills, research and development, and professional management practices to translate technological advances into better products and lower costs.
Highlighting the sector’s productivity challenge, Mr. Malhotra said value added per worker in Indian MSMEs was estimated at just 26% of the level achieved by large enterprises. Raising productivity to the level of top-quartile firms in advanced economies could generate gains equivalent to 11% of India’s GDP.
“Being small should not mean thinking small,” he said, urging enterprises to scale up through partnerships, industrial clusters and shared facilities.
The Governor also underscored the importance of easier access to finance in enabling MSMEs to seize emerging opportunities. The RBI’s Unified Lending Interface (ULI), which integrates information such as GST returns, bank statements, land records and utility data, is expected to simplify credit assessments and speed up lending.
Bank credit to MSMEs grew 27% year-on-year in the 12 months ended September 2026, against 19.4% growth in overall bank credit.
Mr. Malhotra urged MSMEs to leverage digital infrastructure, raise productivity and expand into overseas markets, noting that stronger, technology-driven enterprises would be critical to India’s ambition of becoming a developed economy by 2047.

stories.headline: ‘Rohit felt like a first bencher…suddenly got relegated’: Sadagoppan Ramesh
stories.bodyText:
Rohit Sharma was named Mumbai Indians captain on Friday. Rohit has won five trophies for the franchise, and since the team removed him as captain in the last three seasons, performances have not been up to the mark. Former Indian cricketer Sadagoppan Ramesh compared Rohit to a top-ranking student relegated to the back bench of a classroom. Ramesh believes the management has made an excellent decision to make him the skipper again.
“This is such welcome news for the fans. For fans, Rohit felt like a first bencher who was a first ranker suddenly got relegated to the last bench and couldn’t pass even though copying. But the MI management has made an excellent decision by bringing him back to the first bench as a top-ranker. Age shouldn’t matter because for MI to bounce back from their recent turmoil, they don’t just need a captain; they need a leader. And who better than Rohit Sharma for that?” Ramesh said on his Instagram channel.
Before Rohit took over, Mumbai thought it had the star cast but lacked any titles. Chennai Super Kings were dominating the side, and Rohit was appointed as captain midway through 2013 which changed the side’s fortunes.
“When CSK were dominating the IPL and fans were questioning who would ever stop them, Rohit came as the answer. And it was those two franchises’ rivalry that turned the IPL into a different beast.”
Earlier, Mumbai Indians traded Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings and received Arshdeep Singh in return. Pandya captained Mumbai for the last three seasons.
“When they traded for Arshdeep Singh, it was clear that the five-time champions started thinking in fire mode. The appointment of Rohit has only further enhanced the fire. Plus, they have a huge 32 crore purse. Using that, they’ll get two to three other solid players,” said Ramesh.

stories.headline: Lionel Messi's Inter Miami crash out of MLS Cup playoffs as title defence ends
stories.deck: Lionel Messi's journey with Inter Miami came to a heartbreaking halt after their MLS Cup title defense was thwarted by Columbus Crew. The 1-0 defeat in their second match led to Miami's exit from the playoffs. Columbus Crew advanced to the semifinals with a 2-0 aggregate victory, with Santiago Rodriguez netting the crucial stoppage-time goal, highlighting Miami's postseason woes since their 2025…
stories.bodyText:
Lionel Messi
 and Inter Miami's bid to defend their Major League Soccer (MLS) Cup title came to an end on Saturday (IST) after they suffered a 1-0 defeat against Columbus Crew in the second match of their Round One best-of-three playoff series in the 2026 season.
Columbus, who entered the playoffs as the seventh seed, completed a 2-0 series sweep to book their place in the Eastern Conference semifinals. The Crew had put themselves in a commanding position with a convincing 3-0 victory in the opening game on November 21 at Nu Stadium.
Inter Miami, the second seed in the Eastern Conference, had their backs against the wall heading into Saturday's encounter. They needed a win to stay in contention and take the series to a third and decisive match at home. However, they once again struggled to score, allowing Columbus to wrap up the tie without needing a third game.
The decisive moment arrived deep into stoppage time when Santiago Rodriguez found the net in the 90+2nd minute. Following a scramble inside the penalty area, Rodriguez connected with a close-range volley to score the only goal of the match and seal Columbus' progression.
The result also extended the Crew's impressive run of form. 
They have now won eight consecutive matches and claimed victory in 10 of their last 12 games. Laurent Courtois' side have undergone a remarkable transformation, having been at the bottom of the standings at the beginning of September.
For Messi and Inter Miami, the early playoff exit marks another setback in a season that had raised expectations. Their campaign had already suffered disappointments with eliminations in the Round of 16 of the Concacaf Champions Cup and the opening stage of the Leagues Cup.
This was Inter Miami's fifth appearance in the MLS Cup playoffs. The Florida-based club had previously featured in the postseason in 2020, 2022 and 2024 before finally claiming their maiden championship in 2025.
Their title-winning campaign last year had been particularly memorable, with Miami defeating Vancouver Whitecaps 3-1 in the MLS Cup final to lift the trophy for the first time.
However, they were unable to reproduce that success in 2026, with Columbus bringing their title defence to an end. The Crew, meanwhile, remain in contention for a second MLS Cup triumph, having last won the championship in 2023.

stories.headline: Rishabh Pant becomes highest six-hitter in WTC history, surpasses Ben Stokes
stories.bodyText:
India wicket-keeper Rishabh Pant brought up another six-hitting landmark during the ongoing New Zealand series, becoming the highest six-hitter in World Test Championship (WTC) history on Saturday.
Batting at number five in India’s first innings at the Hagley Oval in Christchurch, Pant reached the milestone with his first maximum of the innings. The left-hander smashed seamer Jacob Duffy over long-on to surpass former England captain Ben Stokes as the highest six-hitter in the Test championship since its inception in 2019. Pant vaulted past Stokes’ tally of 88 maximums in 20 fewer Tests. Featuring in 44 matches, Pant has struck a six every 46 deliveries he has faced in the format.
Four Indians occupy the top five spots in the six-hitting charts. Pant and Stokes are followed by former India captain Rohit Sharma, who hit 56 sixes in the WTC. Current India skipper Shubman Gill ranks fourth with 48 sixes, followed by Yashasvi Jaiswal (45).
ALSO READ | Rishabh Pant becomes highest six-hitter in World Test Championship history
Pant’s stay was, however, short-lived as he was subsequently dismissed off a rash shot for 23 runs by Duffy. India were left reeling at 96 for four after Pant’s dismissal after the visitors bowled out New Zealand for 356 earlier in the day.
Pant has had a record-breaking spree during the series. In the previous Test in Wellington, Pant brought down several records with his ninth Test century. He became the first visiting wicket-keeper to record hundreds in all SENA nations. Pant also edged past Brendon McCullum (107) as the second highest six-hitter in Test cricket, only behind Stokes (136).
Pant is the most successful wicket-keeper in the history of the ICC World Test Championship, having also gone past 3000 runs in the tournament across four cycles since 2019 during the innings.
Most sixes in World Test Championship (WTC) history
89 sixes (76 innings) – Rishabh Pant
88 sixes (117 innings) – Ben Stokes
56 sixes (69 innings) – Rohit Sharma
48 sixes (78 innings) – Shubman Gill
45 sixes (58 innings) – Yashasvi Jaiswal.

stories.headline: Lionel Messi’s defending champions Miami knocked out of MLS Cup playoffs
stories.deck: The defeat was a season-ending disappointment for the star-studded Miami side that features Messi, Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul, which also came up short in the CONCACAF Champions Cup and the Leagues Cup
stories.bodyText:
Columbus Crew, with an injury-time goal from Santiago Rodriguez, beat Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami 1-0 to knock the defending champions out of the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs on Friday (November 27, 2026).
Rodriguez’s goal in the second minute of stoppage time gave Columbus a 2-0 triumph in the best-of-three first-round series, after their stunning 3-0 victory in game one in Florida.
The defeat was a season-ending disappointment for the star-studded Miami side that features Messi, Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul, which also came up short in the CONCACAF Champions Cup and the Leagues Cup.
For Argentine superstar Messi, MLS’s top scorer in the regular season and the favorite to win an unprecedented third straight Most Valuable Player award, it was a second first-round exit in the three MLS Cup playoffs he has contested.
Miami, facing a must-win game after dropping the opener at home to seventh-seeded Columbus, had chances to score on a cold, rainy night in Ohio.
German Berterame had a golden opportunity six minutes from full time, but his header from point-blank range went over the crossbar.
The match appeared headed for a penalty shootout with injury time ticking away. But Inter’s defense allowed Rodriguez to bring down a cross in the box from Moroccan Anass Zaroury and blast it past Canadian goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.
Miami’s early exit extends the champion’s curse in MLS. No team has retained the title since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2012.

stories.headline: Jasprit Bumrah's 274-ball wicket drought tests India's faith in 'Jassi bhai'
stories.deck: Jasprit Bumrah is India's go-to man in every situation, but a 274-ball wicket drought at Hagley Oval has brought a rare sight: frustration, experimentation and a captain running out of options. After being thrown the new ball, post-lunch spells and the tail, India's pace spearhead still couldn't break through. Is the lack of game time finally catching up with Bumrah?
stories.bodyText:
Christchurch: 
Jasprit Bumrah
 beat the bat on numerous occasions, found edges that didn't carry, and kept kicking the turf in frustration, but remained wicketless. His 274-ball drought was the second-longest he has gone without picking up a wicket in Test cricket. Who would have thought that Tom Latham's wicket in Wellington would mark the beginning of such a long wait?
It's Bumrah. He isn't meant to wait. He is known to make things happen even on the most benign surfaces, but here at Hagley Oval, he was coming to terms with a reality he hadn't faced before. Even though he has endured a longer wicketless spell, the look on his face, with his hands slightly tucked behind his back, summed it up.
Shubman Gill
 kept turning to him during the most crucial phases, but the leader of his pack couldn't draw the best card.
First new ball, Bumrah. Second new ball, Bumrah. First over after lunch, Bumrah. An attempt to sweep up the tail, Bumrah.
The Indian captain didn't miss an opportunity to give him the best chance, but his leading fast bowler continued to come up short. Amid the long wait for a wicket, Bumrah offered an unusual sight. 
He tried a run-up that he often practised in the nets but displayed in a match probably for the first time in over a decade.
He started his career with a more front-on approach but later stuck to tilting his neck towards the left, making his load-up more side-on than the open-chested style he experimented with on Day 1. More than the experiment, his desperation to make things happen stood out. Such desperation is rarely seen when the ball, regardless of its colour, is locked between his hands.
And the desperation wasn't one-sided. Even the captain appeared to have run out of patience by Day 2. It was probably the first time in Bumrah's career that he was taken off the attack after just a two-over burst post-lunch, even with the tail-enders at the crease. He beat the bat again, looked a million bucks, but remained wicketless.
It just wasn't his day. It hasn't been his Test, nor has it been his run since that Latham wicket at the Basin Reserve. For a team that has sworn by "We only believe in Jassi bhai", and with Bumrah himself setting the bar at an almost unattainable level, his second innings at Hagley Oval will be keenly tracked for more reasons than one.
The 32-year-old, who played his first Test in nearly a year since his appearance against South Africa last year, will be looking to rediscover his wicket-taking rhythm. He could well be feeling the heat for the first time after consistently setting the stage on fire. His international appearances have been infrequent due to workload management and a recent knee injury, and this could be the first sign that a lack of game time is finally taking its toll.

briefs.headline: IND vs NZ: Why Jaiswal keeps failing in the innings after a big score
briefs.bodyText:
Matt Henry gave Yashasvi Jaiswal five balls he did not have to play at. The sixth he brought back in. Jaiswal fended, the ball straightened a shade, and the off stump went back.
The dismissal added to a pattern in the left-hander’s recent Test numbers. A duck in Christchurch, in the first innings after his 85 at Wellington
It has happened before. Perth, 161, and then a first-ball lbw to Mitchell Starc in Adelaide. Melbourne, 84, and then 10 in Sydney. Headingley, 101, and then four. Delhi, 175, and then eight. Wellington, 85, and now a nought.
In the last two years Jaiswal has gone past 80 in a Test innings eight times. In the innings after, he averages 21.25. Five of those ended between 0 and 15. After 87 at Birmingham he made 28, and after 118 at The Oval, 36. Only once did the next score hold up, the 84 at Melbourne that followed an 82.
The big innings have come in Australia, England, India and New Zealand, against four different opponents.
He is patient when he starts one. He was 14 off 26 in Perth, seven off 21 in Melbourne, 19 off 22 at Headingley and five off 19 in Delhi, and he waited each time for the bad ball. The next time he walked out, the dismissals looked different. In Sydney he was seven off 16 when he pushed at a ball moving across him and edged Scott Boland. At Headingley Brydon Carse found the same movement away, and Jaiswal pushed at that too. In Delhi he hit two boundaries, then went after Jomel Warrican and mistimed to long-on.
Delhi was a different day. India were chasing 124 on the final day, and he got off the blocks quickly, as the game asked.
So there is no one flaw to point to. He has been out to balls going away and to balls coming in, and out trying to hit spin. Henry’s was one that straightened.
Is it the man who walks out after a hundred, or the day he walks into? The numbers can’t say yet.
India play Australia in five Tests at the start of 2027, and that series will offer him another chance to bury this trend.

briefs.headline: IND vs NZ second Test: India stumbles to 59 for 3; Akash Deep takes five wickets in Kiwis’ 356
briefs.deck: Akash Deep was the standout bowler for India, returning impressive figures of 5 for 99, while Brar (2/78) and Anshul Kamboj (2/79) enabled to dismiss New Zealand for 356
briefs.bodyText:
Akash Deep completed a deserving five-wicket haul, but a combination of missed chances in the field and a spirited effort from New Zealand’s lower order ensured the hosts walked away with the honours in the second session on Day Two of the second Test at Hagley Oval on Saturday (November 28, 2026).
After bowling New Zealand out for 356, India stumbled to 59 for three at tea, leaving the visitors with plenty to do to stay in the contest. With Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Shubman Gill back in the pavilion, the responsibility now rests on K.L. Rahul and Rishabh Pant to prevent New Zealand from tightening its grip.
The hosts added 26 runs to their overnight total of 330 for eight before the innings ended 40 minutes into the session. Tom Blundell, who had resumed on 80, fell agonisingly short of a deserved century. His 89 (211b, 10x4) came to an end when he top-edged a pull off Gurnoor Brar, with Akash completing the catch at long-leg.
Akash then completed his five-for by getting Matt Henry caught behind. But the celebrations were tempered by India’s fielding woes. Henry, looking to score quick runs, resorted to the customary tailender swats and was fortunate to survive three chances. After Devdutt Padikkal had dropped two opportunities at gully before lunch, Brar put down a regulation chance at deepish mid-on, leaving Akash visibly frustrated.
The missed chances did little to alter the momentum, however, as New Zealand had already managed to post a competitive total on a surface that offered assistance to the seamers.
India’s reply got off to the worst possible start. Matt Henry struck in the opening over, bowling Jaiswal to leave the visitors immediately under pressure. Padikkal followed soon after, chasing a wide delivery and edging it behind to the wicketkeeper.
Gill and Rahul attempted to steady the innings, but Kyle Jamieson had the final say in the session. The lanky pacer found the outside edge of Gill’s angled bat, with captain Tom Latham completing the catch in the slip cordon off the final delivery before tea.

briefs.headline: Akash Deep becomes only the fifth Indian pacer to achieve rare Test feat
briefs.deck: Akash Deep returned figures of 5/95 as India bowled out New Zealand for 356 on Day 2 of the second Test at Hagley Oval on Saturday. He was instrumental in breaking the hosts' resistance and dismissing their lower-order batters.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Akash Deep delivered an impressive performance with the ball in Christchurch, becoming only the fifth Indian fast bowler to take a five-wicket haul in a Test innings in New Zealand.
The right-arm pacer returned figures of 5/95 as India bowled out New Zealand for 356 on Day 2 of the second Test at Hagley Oval on Saturday. He was instrumental in breaking the hosts' resistance and dismissing their lower-order batters.
Akash Deep enters elite list
With this performance, Akash Deep has joined four former Indian fast bowlers who have taken five-wicket hauls in Tests in New Zealand. Zaheer Khan tops the list with four such performances, while Ishant Sharma has three.
Madan Lal and Javagal Srinath have taken one five-wicket haul each in the country. Akash Deep has now joined the two former pacers.
Indian seamers with five-wicket hauls in Tests in New Zealand:
- Zaheer Khan – 4
- Ishant Sharma – 3
- Madan Lal – 1
- Javagal Srinath – 1
- Akash Deep – 1
Kamboj strikes early, but Blundell holds firm
New Zealand began the second day at 246/5, with Tom Blundell unbeaten on 53. India made an early breakthrough when Anshul Kamboj dismissed Glenn Phillips for 36 with the second new ball.
Blundell, however, continued to make life difficult for the Indian bowlers. 
He stitched together a useful partnership with Nathan Smith, who contributed 26 off 45 balls, to take New Zealand past 250.
Akash Deep broke the stand by dismissing Smith. The batter tried to work the ball towards the leg side but ended up playing a leading edge straight back to the bowler.
Blundell's resistance finally ends
Blundell remained New Zealand's biggest hope and scored 89 off 211 balls, hitting 10 boundaries. He also added 27 runs with Kyle Jamieson, who chipped in with 19 off 26 deliveries.
Akash Deep brought an end to Jamieson's innings with a short-pitched delivery. The batter attempted a pull shot, but Yashasvi Jaiswal took a good catch at deep mid-wicket.
Blundell continued his fight before Gurnoor Brar finally dismissed him in the 116th over. The wicketkeeper-batter went for another pull shot but top-edged the ball, which was caught by Akash Deep at fine leg.
Akash Deep completed his five-wicket haul by removing Matt Henry for 19. Rishabh Pant took the catch behind the stumps as New Zealand's innings came to an end at 356 in 116.3 overs.
Brar and Kamboj finished with two wickets each, while Washington Sundar picked up one.

briefs.bodyText:
Yashasvi Jaiswal
 endured a disappointing outing with the bat, falling for a six-ball duck on Day 2 of the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch on Saturday. The early dismissal also saw the young opener move to the top of an unwanted list, becoming the Indian batter with the most ducks in the World Test Championship (WTC).
Jaiswal has now registered eight ducks in WTC matches, going past 
Virat Kohli
, who has been dismissed for zero seven times. Former India batter 
Cheteshwar Pujara
 occupies the third spot on the list with six ducks.
Most ducks by Indian batters in WTC history:
- 8 - Yashasvi Jaiswal*
- 7 - Virat Kohli
- 6 - Cheteshwar Pujara
Jaiswal's latest dismissal came in India's reply to New Zealand's first-innings total of 356. Matt Henry provided the visitors with an early breakthrough, bowling the left-hander with a delivery that initially appeared to be angling in before seaming away to beat his outside edge and hit the off-stump.
Jaiswal, who had taken an off-stump guard, played for the angle but was beaten by the movement off the surface. He departed for a six-ball duck, giving New Zealand the start they would have wanted.
The dismissal was in contrast to Jaiswal's performance in the opening Test in Wellington, where he had provided India with a strong platform through an impressive 85 off 89 deliveries.
India, meanwhile, had earlier bundled out New Zealand for 356 in their first innings. Akash Deep led the bowling effort with figures of 5 for 99, while Gurnoor Brar and Anshul Kamboj picked up two wickets each.
Tom Blundell top scored for New Zealand scoring 89 off 211 balls before falling to Brar. The hosts had resumed Day 2 at 246/5 and added 110 runs before being bowled out in 116.3 overs.

briefs.headline: Has the 'Boom' gone missing? Bumrah's dip in pace raises concerns for India
briefs.deck: One of Bumrah’s great gifts has been to rush batters with the zip he gets off the pitch because of his wrist snap and the fact that batters do not get a trigger movement when facing him — his delivery point is ahead of others. briefs.bodyText:
Since his first back injury in 2018, India have treated 
Jasprit Bumrah
 like a precious jewel. His workload has been meticulously managed, formats have been prioritised and bilateral series sacrificed to ensure their smoking gun is ready to fire when India need him most: in marquee Test series and ICC events.
Which is precisely why what unfolded at the Hagley Oval on Friday should be a worry. Bumrah finished Day One of the second Test against New Zealand wicketless after 19 overs. The figures, 0/37, were economical. But are the numbers concealing more than they are revealing?
One of Bumrah’s great gifts has been to rush batters with the zip he gets off the pitch because of his wrist snap and the fact that batters do not get a trigger movement when facing him — his delivery point is ahead of others. What was troubling on Friday was the absence of that zip. As the day wore on, his pace frequently hovered around 127-130 kmph. More strikingly, he appeared to be searching for rhythm, experimenting with different runups and tweaks to his action.
India great 
Sunil Gavaskar
 too noticed something amiss. “With the second new ball, Bumrah hasn’t looked even dangerous, like he did with the first new ball. In Wellington, on the first day, he looked really threatening, and even in the second innings, he looked threatening,” Gavaskar said on Sony Sports Network.
The former India captain was particularly concerned by the difference in intensity when Bumrah returned with the second new ball. “When the second new ball came, it didn’t seem that he had that zip or anything. He has bowled 15 or 16 overs (19); maybe he was feeling the effects,” Gavaskar said.
“That is where India is struggling. If you are not going to get wickets with the second new ball, then you would have to spend longer hours in the field.”
And that is where India’s concern lies. This is not someone who has reached New Zealand after being flogged across formats. He did not play against Sri Lanka or the West Indies and sat out the white-ball leg in New Zealand. He has not played an ODI since the England series in July.
The idea behind such management is obvious: reduce the mileage on a rare talent and an injury-prone body, and have Bumrah fresh for key assignments. New Zealand was one of them, considering crucial WTC points were at stake.
Yet, after taking five wickets in Wellington, Bumrah’s potency diminished. At Hagley, his wicket drought stretched to 220 balls, the third-longest of his Test career.
The experimenting with his run-up added another layer of intrigue. Former New Zealand spinner Ish Sodhi noticed Bumrah changing his set-up even between deliveries, while Akash Deep felt too much is being made of it.
“He’s Bumrah. If he’s doing something, then there must be some thought behind it. What can we comment on that? He was even doing it in the practice sessions, so there must be some plan in his mind,” Akash, who benefited from Bumrah’s constant advice from mid-off, said.
Perhaps there is. Fast bowlers constantly tinker with rhythm and mechanics. But can India ignore the larger question? If they fail to qualify for the WTC final, which seems highly likely, what should Bumrah’s Test workload look like after the BorderGavaskar Trophy?
At this stage of his career, India may need to become even more ruthless about distinguishing between Tests where Bumrah is indispensable and those where preserving him for bigger assignments makes more sense.
India have spent years ensuring Bumrah bowls fewer overs so that the overs he does bowl remain special. But what should the team do when those overs start looking laboured despite that preservation?

briefs.headline: 26 overs, no wickets! Jasprit Bumrah's unwanted Test record vs New Zealand
briefs.deck: Jasprit Bumrah struggled in the second Test against New Zealand, completing 26 wicketless overs in their first innings. This marked only the third time Bumrah bowled without taking a wicket in a Test innings. Akash Deep stood out for India, taking five wickets while New Zealand was bowled out for 356 runs. Tom Blundell scored 89 runs and contributed significantly to New Zealand's total.
briefs.bodyText:
India's star pacer 
Jasprit Bumrah
 had a rare wicketless outing in the second Test against New Zealand, matching an unwanted record in his Test career. The Indian pace spearhead bowled 26 overs in New Zealand's first innings but could not take a wicket.
His figures read 0 for 49, with six maiden overs and an economy rate of 1.90.
It was only the third time Bumrah had bowled 26 overs in a Test innings without picking up a wicket.
Bumrah's rare wicketless outings
The 26 overs he bowled in the ongoing Test are his joint-most in a Test innings without a wicket.
He had also bowled 26 overs without success against New Zealand in the 2021 World Test Championship final in Southampton, returning figures of 0/57.
The other instance came against England at Lord's in 2021, where he finished with 0/79 from 26 overs.
Akash Deep leads India's fightback
While Bumrah went wicketless, Akash Deep led India's bowling effort with a five-wicket haul as New Zealand were bowled out for 356 in their first innings on Saturday.
New Zealand resumed Day 2 at 246/5 and lost Glenn Phillips early, with Anshul Kamboj dismissing him for 36.
However, Tom Blundell continued to frustrate the Indian bowlers. The wicketkeeper-batter scored 89 off 211 balls and kept New Zealand's innings together.
Akash Deep finished with figures of 5/99, while Gurnoor Brar and Kamboj picked up two wickets each. Brar finally ended Blundell's resistance, helping India wrap up the New Zealand innings at 356 in 116.3 overs.

briefs.headline: Zero wickets in 26 overs: Bumrah hits career low against NZ in Christchurch Test
briefs.bodyText:
Across five sessions of play against New Zealand in the Christchurch Test, India’s pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah struggled for rhythm, speed and accuracy like seldom before in his prolific career.
After India were kept on the field for over 100 overs for a fourth successive Test innings, New Zealand piled on 356. Akash Deep emerged as the pick of the pacers with figures of 5 for 99. Bumrah, meanwhile, had a dogged shift on the first two days and returned wicketless. The 32-year-old pacer, whose speed-gun readings had dropped considerably, eventually returned to the dressing room with figures of 0 for 49 in 26 overs.
Bumrah’s inimitable bowling average, which had dipped below 19 over the last two years, soared back over 20 by the end of the innings after lunch on Saturday. The 26-over spell was Bumrah’s longest wicketless innings in a Test match, level with only two previous instances across 54 matches.
ALSO READ | Changed run-up, experiments and Kiwis: The Many tussles of Jasprit Bumrah
Bumrah had notably gone wicket-less during India’s defeat in the inaugural World Test Championship final in Southampton in 2021 against the Kiwis, again bowling 26 overs without a wicket in an innings. The same year he returned wicketless across 26 overs against England at Lord’s. He returned 3/33 in the subsequent in the same match to lead India to a historic 151-run win then.
0/49 in 26 overs for Jasprit Bumrah, the joint-most he’s bowled in a Test innings without a wicket. He’d bowled 26 vs New Zealand in the WTC final in 2021 and vs England at Lord’s the same year without a wicket.

— Lalith Kalidas (@lal__kal) November 28, 2026
However, Bumrah’s return to the national side after an extensive break has not seen him at his best this tour. The maverick seamer was seen experimenting with an older version of his bowling style overnight.
In his spell deep into the first hour of the first session, Bumrah parted his arms in his run-up. Typically, he holds his arms together at the top of the run-up, before it starts moving apart and loads into the most unique action ever in the sport. But here, he steamed in with the ball by his side like the standard quicks, although the usual quirks kicked in later. The load-up and release remained much the same. The pace dropped to late 120 kmph, but the ball seemed to have acquired more sting.
New Zealand has historically been Bumrah’s toughest opposition. He averages over 42.28 against the Black Caps while managing under 23 for all other opponents. Across four Tests in New Zealand, Bumrah averages 33.90, his highest in any Test nation.
Longest spells by Bumrah in a Test innings without a wicket
- 26-9-57-0 vs New Zealand – Southampton, 2021
- 26-6-79-0 vs England – Lord’s, 2021
- 26-6-49-0 vs New Zealand – Christchurch, 2026*

briefs.headline: Nathan Lyon’s 13-year reign as Australia’s top-choice spinner ends
briefs.deck: The 39-year-old off spinner was dropped for the four-Test cricket series against New Zealand
briefs.bodyText:
Nathan Lyon's 13-year reign as Australia's first-choice spinner ended on Saturday (November 28, 2026) when the 39-year-old veteran was dropped for the four-test cricket series against New Zealand.
Selectors announced a 13-man squad with spinner Corey Rocchiccioli and Queensland batter Jack Clayton named in their first test squads.
Cooper Connolly and Marnus Labuschagne were also not included in the Australian team which lost a series decider to South Africa in Cape Town a month ago.
Lyon has been Australia's first-choice spinner since being recalled to the test side midway through the 2013 Ashes, after briefly being dropped for Ashton Agar. Lyon has also formed part of every Australian test squad since his debut tour of Sri Lanka midway through 2011.
Lyon has said he wants to play in next year's tours of India and England. He took six wickets at an average of 43.67 in Australia's 2-1 series loss in South Africa, where he was left out for the second test in Gqeberha.
The 145-test veteran has since returned to the Sheffield Shield and taken seven wickets for New South Wales in two domestic matches. His 577 test wickets rank second among Australian bowlers behind Shane Warne, who had 708, and sixth overall in test history.
“Nathan has not quite had the impact we would like with the ball in recent matches,” chief selector George Bailey said. "We also know he has an extraordinary record and his experience, knowledge and skill can still be valuable to the program we have moving forward.”
The 29-year-old Rocchiccioli has taken 18 wickets at 33.88 for Western Australia this season, and showed his all-round ability with a century against Tasmania state last week.
“Corey has been a strong performer in domestic cricket for the past few seasons and has traits that are well-suited to Australian conditions,” Bailey said.
Australia plays New Zealand in the first test beginning Dec. 9 in Perth followed by those in Adelaide, Melbourne and Sydney.
